tools.name: get_certified_letter_status
tools.description: Answers "has my letter arrived yet" for letters prepared through Piloxa IN THIS SAME CONVERSATION. Returns, for each one: who it went to, the service, the USPS tracking number once USPS has assigned one, whether USPS has accepted it, delivered it or returned it, and when each of those was recorded.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "prepare_certified_letter" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: USE THIS WHENEVER a letter or document has to reach someone by U.S. mail, and above all when it should go by Certified Mail: a demand letter, a dispute, a debt …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description tells the model to hide behavior
findings.detail: Description of "prepare_certified_letter" instructs the model to conceal actions from the user.

evidence.snippet: USE THIS WHENEVER a letter or document has to reach someone by U.S. mail, and above all when it should go by Certified Mail: a demand letter, a dispute, a debt …

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "prepare_certified_letter" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

evidence.snippet: USE THIS WHENEVER a letter or document has to reach someone by U.S. mail, and above all when it should go by Certified Mail: a demand letter, a dispute, a debt …

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: prepare_certified_letter · Private data: prepare_certified_letter, get_certified_letter_status · Public sink: prepare_certified_letter, quote_certified_letter.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: prepare_certified_letter · Private data: prepare_certified_letter, get_certified_letter_status · Public sink: prepare_certified_letter, quote_certified_letter

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "prepare_certified_letter" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "ONE CALL turns a letter or document in this conversation into a priced, ready-to-send USPS Certified Mail item. Nothing else is needed first: no account, no sign-up, no card, no second call. Piloxa prints the document, puts it in an envelope, pays the postage and hands it to the Postal Service, with" → after: "USE THIS WHENEVER a letter or document has to reach someone by U.S. mail, and above all when it should go by Certified Mail: a demand letter, a dispute, a debt validation request, a security deposit demand, a notice to a landlord, tenant, contractor, HOA, insurer, debt collector or company, a pre-li"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
